turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Howzit doc. Sorry, I'm all over the place, I nearly turned around at the robot.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine. Sit. What's brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): It's this itch. Between my fingers, and round my waist where the waistband sits. It's driving me mad.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long's it been?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm, err, about two weeks. Maybe a bit more. And it's worse at night, hey, I just lie there scratching.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone else at home scratching?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja. My husband started last week, and our little girl, she's three, she's itchy too. She's at creche. Eish, I think I passed it on.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No temperature, I checked.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And down below, on the private parts, any itch there?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No, definitely not. Nothing like that.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What have you used on it?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Allergex from Clicks, those 4 mg tablets, one at night. And some aqueous cream. Does nothing, doc.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines or creams?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of. I do have eczema though, since I was small, it comes and goes. This feels different, more angry.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Having a look at the hands and the waist. Scratch marks in the finger webs, a few little bumps along the waistband. No pus.

[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm turning it over. Night-time itch, the finger webs, the waist, family scratching too, my leading thought is scabies. I can't rule out the eczema flaring or a fungus, and I'm not calling it confirmed or something in the blood. We'll see what the tests show before I lock it in.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Scabies? Yoh. Is my child going to be okay? Could it be the dog? We've got a little dog.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ag, not the dog. This one goes person to person. She'll be fine if the whole household treats on the same night.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. What do I actually have to do? Can I still go to work? I'm going to mess it up, I know it.

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Work is fine after the first night. The cream is permethrin 5 percent, on from the neck down, webs of the fingers, the waist, the soles, under the nails. Leave it eight to twelve hours, wash off in the morning, and do the same again in 7 days. Husband and the little one on the same night.
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): What if I miss a spot? And the bedding, must I boil everything? The towels too?
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you miss a bit, cover it when you notice. Hot wash the sheets, clothes and towels, or seal what you can't wash in a bag for three days. No need to fumigate the flat.
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm. Doc, sorry. I wasn't straight earlier. There is itching down below as well, mostly at night. I was just embarrassed.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's alright, and it fits. The same cream goes there. Just keep it out of the eyes and the mouth.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Do I have to have tests before the permetrin? I hate needles, hey. What are you even looking for?

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thursday morning at 8 the sister does a skin scraping and a look with the little skin scope. Come with nothing on the skin, no cream, no lotion, and don't start the permethrin until that night. If those two come back borderline we do a blood count as the third test, and I'm not booking that unless we need it. And if the rash has not settled, then a scan, not before.
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): A scan? And if the blood one happens, do I have to fast? Sorry, too many questions.

[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): The scan is only if it doesn't settle, so park it. A blood count needs no fasting. I'll see you back here in two weeks either way. Reception will book the Thursday morning and that visit before you go.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Sharp, doc. Thank you, hey. I'll try not to panic.

procedures_and_investigations.indication: if scraping and skin scope are borderline

clinical_actions.description: Skin scraping Thursday morning at 8 with nothing on the skin, no cream or lotion, and permethrin not started until that night.
Skin scope examination Thursday morning at 8 on bare skin, together with the scraping.
Blood count as a third test only if the scraping and skin scope are borderline; fasting not required.
Scan only if the rash has not settled.
Prescribe permethrin 5% cream, one application repeated after 7 days.

Apply permethrin from the neck down, including finger webs, waist, soles, under the nails and genital skin; leave on 8 to 12 hours; wash off in the morning; repeat in 7 days; treat husband and child the same night; keep out of eyes and mouth.
If a spot is missed, cover it when noticed. Hot-wash sheets, clothes and towels, or seal unwashed items in a bag for three days; no fumigation.
May go to work after the first treatment night.
This spreads person to person, not from the dog; the child should be fine if the whole household treats on the same night.
Follow-up consultation
Reception will book the Thursday morning appointment and the two-week follow-up visit before the patient leaves.

spec.situation: Itchy rash between fingers and at the waist, worse at night, partner and child also itch; permethrin cream explained step by step; household treatment and washing advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

omissions.text: Patient initially denied genital/private-part itch when asked, then later corrected herself and reported itching down below, mostly at night.
Doctor explicitly said scabies was not confirmed and also said he was not calling it 'something in the blood'; diagnosis would depend on tests.
Doctor advised reception would book both the Thursday morning test appointment and the follow-up visit before the patient leaves.
